steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Who's there?
Me, me!
I thought you would have gotten used to me now, but then I remembered I haven't ever spoken to you like this before. Or have I? I don't remember.
Like a cloud drifting down from the night sky—
A furry creature appears before Adele, spinning slowly in the air.
It lands on a mailbox by the roadside, looking both graceful and comical.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Oh—

steps.name: Strange Creature
steps.text: Hello? Good evening?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: ...Little Black Sheep?

steps.name: Strange Creature
steps.text: You're calling me Little Black Sheep? Sure, I guess.

steps.name: Strange Creature
steps.text: Why the look of surprise? We've met. I mean, we have, haven't we?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Sorry, I... I didn't know you could talk.

steps.name: Strange Creature
steps.text: We don't talk often. I mean, I'm the only one who can. The rest of us, well, maybe they don't like interacting with people. Or maybe they haven't learned to yet?

steps.name: Strange Creature
steps.text: Anyway, that's not important. I've found you now, so I can just talk to you.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: You... you know me?

steps.name: Strange Creature
steps.text: I guess you could say I watched you grow up?

steps.name: Strange Creature
steps.text: Now, no, I don't peep at private lives. It's just, well, pure and simple companionship. Anyway, what I mean to say is, of course I know you.

steps.name: Strange Creature
steps.text: I don't know if it's a coincidence that I ran into you here, but it's an opportunity.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: I'm sorry... I don't quite understand.

steps.name: Strange Creature
steps.text: Of course, puny humans always have so many questions. Don't worry, I'll answer.

steps.name: Strange Creature
steps.text: Let's have a little chat. Do you have time for that? I'm not sure if girls your age need to be home by a certain time or not.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: I'm not a kid anymore!

steps.name: Strange Creature
steps.text: Good, then you have time. Want to go for a walk?

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: Water hole, hot springs, white smoke.

steps.name: Boy
steps.text: That's wrong! The smoke from the volcano is gray. Siesta isn't like this.

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: But that's not Siesta anymore.

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: Siesta is where we are right now. Those big tall buildings all have white smoke.

steps.name: Boy
steps.text: This is Siesta, but that Siesta is Siesta too.

steps.name: Boy
steps.text: I know, let's call it Old Siesta!

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: This Siesta is the child of Old Siesta.

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: Old Siesta is like Dad. It's far away from us right now... but it'll come back, and it'll bring gifts for us!

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: What would you want?

steps.name: Boy
steps.text: Enis!

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: Are you off work?

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Shh, be quiet, Harley is sleeping.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Do you remember what I told you the last time, kids?

steps.name: Boy
steps.text: Don't go out at night, don't go to the plates outside the nomadic city...

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: And don't draw on anything but drawing paper...

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Now, who's the great artist who painted the portrait of 'Herman Shell-Brain' on the restaurant's back wall?

steps.name: Boy
steps.text: But all the grown ups call him that...

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Well... grown ups aren't always right. That's why it means something for the three of us to go on adventures. We find treasures that they don't.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Before that, though, we're going to clean the wall tomorrow, right?

steps.name: Boy
steps.text: Right...

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Then, for good kids who admit their mistakes—
The young man extends a hand, three finely made clay dolls with lifelike expressions lying in his palm, just like the smiles in the family photo on the table.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: One for each member of our adventure team.

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: Where did you get this?

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: I made it. Like I said, I know magic.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: You don't like it?

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: (Liberi, Feline, Perro...)

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: (Why are all of them different?)

steps.name: Boy
steps.text: I wish I got a 'D32 Steel Warrior' instead.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Special gifts are for special days. Don't worry, all that you want is waiting in the future.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Now, it's bedtime.

steps.name: Boy
steps.text: When can we go back to Old Siesta, Enis?

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Not yet. It gets really grumpy and breathes fire if you wake it up.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Give it time, and maybe it'll be in a better mood. Then we can go and find it together.

steps.name: Boy
steps.text: I want to be an adventurer like dad!

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: We're even better than that. We're an adventure team.

steps.name: Boy
steps.text: We're an adventure team! Enis, you should take us to dig up those black rocks!

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Listen, you promised not to tell anyone that I went to dig up black rocks. That's a secret, you know.

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: Will you take us to Old Siesta's beach park?

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: I don't know if there will be much left of it... but I can take you to another amusement park.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: There are water parks elsewhere too. You've seen them in Dad's photos, haven't you?

steps.name: Boy
steps.text: Volcano AND water park! It's a promise!

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Yup, a promise between the members of the adventure team.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: Goods from the Columbian partners have been loaded. On the Leithanien side...

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: And I have to survey the layout of the trade fair venue...

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: It's getting rather late, Young Master. You should get some rest. You don't have to do everything yourself.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: I can't just sit around doing nothing...

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: The residents aren't too excited about a logistics hub. Maybe the international trade fair will change their attitude.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: As an independent city state, Siesta has enormous potential in leveraging its position as a transportation hub.

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: It's hard for one in the middle of all this to understand one's place in changes like these. They have their minds full worrying about a new life in which they don't know what to expect.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: I know. I remember how I cried when we moved from Minos when I was little.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: Change is always scary. I want to make it easier on everyone.

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: I understand you met with Miss Swire today.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: ...I did.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: We couldn't reach a consensus, but the conversation helped remind me...

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: Messenger or merchant, the power to change lives comes with great responsibility.

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: Are you sure this responsibility is yours to bear?

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: Your father has high hopes for you, but he did not ask you to shoulder such responsibility so early.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: I will never leave his shadow if I only do what he wants me to.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: The Siesta project is important to him. There's never been a better chance to realize the dream he had when he established MountainDash Logistics.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: MountainDash is based in Lungmen, and bound by the rules of the Federation of Enterprises. He faces difficulty when it comes to the Siestan subsidiary.

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: Your father told me he expects you to be ready to take over his work in five years, and that he has already started planning his retirement in Rim Billiton.

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: Perhaps he should accelerate those plans.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: Now you're just teasing me...

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: Still, it would be good for Father to spend more time with Mother.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: Thanks, Butler. Don't worry about me. I want to get this done while I'm focused.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Enjoying yourself?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: I had tons of local food and tried the artificial hot springs here! I guess they have the same effects as real volcanic hot springs. It was so good!

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: I didn't get to see the legendary Obsidian Festival, but I had a great time taking in the passionate atmosphere!

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Very nice. Sounds like New Siesta has a lot of business potential.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Say, did you feel like you were being watched out there?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Watched?

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: No need to get anxious, just asking.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: I completely understand if that wasn't exactly at the top of your mind.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: A-Are you here in Siesta on a secret mission?

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Mission? What mission? Like I said, I'm here on vacation.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: I don't deal with the L.G.D. often, but I've heard stories about you, why you joined the L.G.D., and...

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: And your family... I can imagine how hard the decision was for you.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: I shouldn't have talked to those reporters.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: It's always the same thing. Getting kidnapped by terrorists when you're little is not exactly something you boast about.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: I hear you've basically been in charge of the L.G.D. ever since Superintendent Ch'en left two years ago.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: I don't exactly understand why you're here in Siesta now, representing your family as an investor.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: And the people who followed us today were from Lungmen too, weren't they?

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Well, you've got me there.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: What do you think about Lungmen, Snowsant?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Well... it's my home.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: I've seen how it changed from when I left Lungmen to study in Columbia, and in the years since I returned.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: As an engineer, it makes me glad to see one skyscraper rise after another, firm and solid.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Firm and solid, yes... a little too much so.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: It's hard for new life to get the sun and nutrition it needs when tall skyscrapers block the light.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Do you mean...?

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Forget it. I'm just babbling.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Don't tell anyone what I just said to you.
It seemed a very long walk.
The massive creature plods forward slowly, quietly. Adele follows behind it, rubbing her eyes from time to time.
One step, two steps. Adele walks forward, stepping on her own shadow. The other passersby seem completely oblivious to the massive creature. Is this real, or just a dream?

steps.name: Strange Creature
steps.text: What are you looking at, girl?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: N-Nothing...

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Aren't we going for a walk? To... where exactly?

steps.name: Strange Creature
steps.text: We're almost there.

steps.name: Strange Creature
steps.text: Look up.
One, two, three... a little creature stops and lifts its head in the light of the streetlamps.
Furry creatures leap and roll on the unfinished plate in the pale moonlight.
Four, five, six...
Little bits of wool drift in the air, under the scattered lamp light.
Almost like sparks, falling in this summer night that no one knows about.
Seven, eight, nine...
They leap across the container in orderly file, leaving marks on the metal with their hooves...

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: A-Are all these Little Black Sheep?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Mr. Little... I mean, Mr. Big Black Sheep...

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Er...

steps.name: Strange Creature
steps.text: Oh, I haven't introduced myself yet, have I?

steps.name: Strange Creature
steps.text: I may be a lot older than you are, but you can call me by my name. It's Dolly.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Mr. Dolly...?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: People in fairy tales always see strange things when they're about to die...

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: Really? How tasteless! That's the kind of stories parents tell their kids these days?

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: Don't worry, girl, it's not your time yet.

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: How have you been? Ah, maybe not the best question... I can see you're not too well. Not in terms of health, at least.

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: But there's nothing that can be done about it... I'm sorry.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Mutti said that the little sheep around me are a gift from her. Did she ask you to stay by my side?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Did you know my parents?

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: It's a little hard to explain just who these little guys are. Let's call them my clones.

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: They all have some special link to this world, and they have different personalities. The fact that they're willing to stay by your side means you're a likeable girl.

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: As for your parents, of course I knew them.

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: I remember that young couple from Leithanien, who wanted to conquer all the volcanoes across the globe.

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: I have to say that, for humans, trying to achieve something regarding 'everything' in the world is a fool's errand.

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: But it's different when it comes to volcanoes. It's a classy dream.

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: Stubborn, but smart, with a real eye for beauty! Especially your mother. I haven't met many people wiser than her.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Were you by their side when... at the end?

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: Ah, now that's a topic not to be spoken of lightly...

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: It was very much a surprise. No one knew the volcano would erupt there and then. But could puny humans really come to know everything about the globe?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Do you feel any sadness about it?

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: Thank goodness you aren't asking me why I didn't save them.

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: I love volcanoes, of course. Surfing on molten lava is the second best thing on the planet.

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: But volcanoes took the lives of two of my friends. It's the eleventh worst thing to happen in recent years.

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: We all want to prevent bad things from happening, but I'm not as omnipotent as I look. There are many things I can't do.

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: If you're really sad, though, you can rub yourself against my wool. That often helps when you're feeling down.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Thank you...

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: Anyway.

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: The past isn't truly over. They're always by your side, in one way or another.
Human and beast sit by the seashore, feeling the caress of the warm sea breeze, and listening to the soft clashing of the waves.
The furry pack of beasts quietly play their game, leaping back and forth on containers and scaffolds, humming contentedly from time to time.
One little beast tries to climb the container, following the herd in front, but fails repeatedly.

steps.name: Tiny Creature
steps.text: (Wistful moan)

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: Sorry, it's been so long since I've sat down for a chat with a human. My vocabulary is limited, so I'll dispense with the formalities.

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: Rather than ask questions that have obvious answers, what I want to ask is—are you happy, little one?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: I... I'm trying to finish my parents' research. It's hard work, but it feels meaningful.

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: So you're not happy.

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: We met in Siesta, as fate would have it. Let's make a deal.

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: Wait, is that the right word in your language? 'Deal?' Maybe I should use a more friendly word... let's say, 'game.'

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: Anyway, I want you to find a few things for me that I lost in Siesta. Consider it a treasure hunt.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: What is it that you lost?

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: Let me think. The North Wind, a seed, and a fur.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: What... do you mean by those?

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: Where's the fun in a game if you know the solution beforehand? Don't be too eager to seek an answer. Feel it out.

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: It'll be worth your while, I promise. I'll have something for you when you find all three.

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: Hm... how about that which you have been seeking?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: What I've been seeking?

a.text: 'I just can't accept the mysterious circumstances surrounding their deaths.'

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: North Wind, seed, fur. Good hunting!
